rule: descending parent-conference full-event start; shared by main conference and workshops

events.caveat: Scheduled future event as of 2026-10-15. Canonical range is the official main Sydney event: expo December 6, tutorials December 7, main conference December 8–10, workshops/competitions December 11–12. Atlanta and Paris satellite events have different ranges, December 9–13. Use the one canonical main-event start 2026-12-06 for all generic NeurIPS 2026 conference/workshop catalogue entries; do not substitute notification dates or individual workshop dates.

Scheduled future event as of 2026-10-15. Tutorials/Industry Day/PhD Symposium November 7; workshops/AnalytiCup November 8; main conference November 9–11. Use 2026-11-07 for both conference and workshop entries. Event dates are distinct from August acceptance notifications.
Official full event August 9–13; workshop/tutorial days August 9–10 and main conference days August 11–13. Use 2026-08-09 for both conference and workshop entries.
Tutorials/expo July 6; main conference July 7–9; workshops July 10–11. Full official event range. Use 2026-07-06 for both conference and workshop entries.

Current official homepage and event page specify May 4–8. All satellite workshops and tutorials were on May 4. An older official CFP PDF says May 3–8; the current homepage and final workshop/tutorial schedules are used instead. Use 2026-05-04 for both conference and workshop entries.

Official homepage gives May 2–5. Main program was May 2–4 and inaugural workshops May 5. The Dates page has stale weekday labels; official workshop call and calendar corroborate the numeric dates. May 1 was advance registration only, outside the advertised event range. Use 2026-05-02 for both conference and workshop entries.
Main conference April 23–25; workshops April 26–27. Full official event range. Use 2026-04-23 for both conference and workshop entries.
Full official event range, including pre-conference activities and post-conference workshops; main technical sessions were January 22–25. Use 2026-01-20 for both conference and workshop entries.

Canonical range is the San Diego event: expo/tutorials December 2, conference sessions December 3–5, workshops December 6–7. The Mexico City event ran November 30–December 5. Use the one canonical main-event start 2025-12-02 for generic NeurIPS 2025 conference/workshop catalogue entries; satellite/location-specific ranges are not used as different keys.

Official homepage gives November 4–9. Program confirms registration/reception November 4, main sessions November 5–7, workshops/tutorials November 8–9. Registration page describes November 5–9, but the full advertised event includes November 4. Use 2025-11-04 for both conference and workshop entries.
Official overall conference July 27–August 1: tutorials/reception July 27, main conference July 28–30, workshops July 31–August 1. Use 2025-07-27 for both conference and workshop entries.

Expo July 13, tutorials July 14, conference sessions July 15–17, workshops July 18–19. Homepage, Dates page, CFP, and visa information agree on July 13–19. A fact-sheet PDF says July 13–20; prefer the explicit operational schedule and consistent official event pages. Use 2025-07-13 for both conference and workshop entries.
Conference sessions April 24–26; workshops April 27–28. Full official event range. Use 2025-04-24 for both conference and workshop entries.

Official IEEE Signal Processing Society event listing gives April 6–11, Hyderabad. The conference website itself was robots-blocked to the research tool, so the organizing society's primary-source listing is used. Use 2025-04-06 for both conference and workshop entries.

Keep TSALM in this group with shared start December 10. Final NeurIPS workshop schedule and organizers' site place TSALM on December 15: https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/events/workshop and https://tsalm-workshop.github.io/neurips-2024/. OpenReview group metadata says December 14, but final event schedules agree on December 15; either is within parent range.

Includes Undergraduate Consortium in the parent event group. Its official call lists August 25–29 with exact day TBA: https://www.kdd.org/kdd2024/call-for-undergraduate-consortium/. Do not use its June 13 decision date.
Official full-event range, including Expo, tutorials, and workshops. Use July 21 as the shared conference/workshop grouping date.
Official full-event range; December 10 is industry expo. Use the official parent start, not main-paper session dates.

Official header, footer, and final program give October 17–21; one homepage body sentence inconsistently says October 17–22. Keep AMLTS grouped at October 17. Published workshop proceedings confirm AMLTS on October 21, within the parent range: https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3375/. An older EasyChair CFP says October 24, inconsistent with final program/proceedings, so it is not adopted.
Keep MiLeTS in this parent event group with shared start August 14. Workshop organizers specify August 15, within the parent range: https://kdd-milets.github.io/milets2022/.
Official dates explicitly label April 25–29 as Conference Sessions & Workshops. Virtual conference.
Official conference-date field explicitly says December 7–8, 2017; author notification October 22 is a separate field.
Official event range. Detailed program confirms workshop day December 12 followed by days through December 15: https://icdm2016.eurecat.cat/detailed-program/.
Official IAPR archive lists the 23rd International Conference on Pattern Recognition in Cancun on December 4–8, 2016, with December 4 workshops included in this range.
Official full conference range. This includes the post-conference company tour on August 16; use parent event start August 12.

These are verified parent AAAI-94 event dates, used for grouping, not a claim that WS-94-01 ran this entire range. Official AAAI report index identifies WS-94-01 as Case-Based Reasoning, David W. Aha, Program Chair; Knowledge Discovery in Databases is WS-94-03: https://new.aaai.org/Press/Reports/Workshops/workshop-reports.php. Exact WS-94-01 workshop day was not independently verified from a readable primary source; do not invent one.
